name: Sous Vide Barbecue Pulled Pork Shoulder Kenji
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt makes the case for cooking pork shoulder sous vide on two grounds: it is hands-off compared with babysitting a smoker all day, and it reaches textures traditional methods cannot. Collagen breaks down with both heat and time, but hotter meat squeezes out more moisture, so a low, stable bath buys tenderness without the loss; he tested a range and landed on 165F for 18 to 24 hours for shreddable-but-moist pork, with 145F for the same span giving a firmer, sliceable roast, while 200F shreds instantly but goes dry. Smoke can come from liquid smoke or smoked salt in the bag, or from a real session over wood afterwards, which he prefers for convenience even though smoke adheres better to raw meat. A pinch of pink curing salt in the rub fakes the cosmetic smoke ring, and the shoulder still needs 90 minutes in a 300F oven or on the grill to build bark.
comment_digest: The strongest thread is what the post-bath finish costs you. One cook found the pork superb straight from the bag but noticeably drier and less supple after 90 minutes in the oven and says he will stop at the bath next time; another crisps individual portions in a pan instead, and a third skips bark entirely, trading caramelised bits for tenderness. One reviewer goes further and says not to sous vide before grilling at all, because his 22-hour 165F shoulder fell apart before it reached the grate, cutting against the author's preference for smoking afterwards. Successful reports stay close to the recipe: 24 hours at 165F, ice bath, overnight in the fridge, then about two hours over apple wood. Two useful tweaks: trim the fat cap and bag it alongside the meat for a crisper, less greasy bark, and chill the bag juices, skim the fat, and stir the gelatin back into the shredded pork.
flags: Comments truncated at 'Read More'. One reviewer's reheating instructions are internally inconsistent about the oven time, so his numbers were not reported. The recipe was not tested by commenters at the 145F sliceable setting in any visible review.
